title: Console surface map and journey icons for sidebar & workspace flows
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: As usage grows, the Console’s left rail has become crowded and inconsistent across dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Engineers and PMs report discovery friction when switching workspaces or finding rollout controls and cost analytics. Goal: Produce a consolidated surface map and a set of journey icons that clarify hierarchy, reduce cognitive load, and speed up common flows (workspace switch, open rollout, cost drilldown). Deliverables: low and high fidelity prototypes, design tokens for iconography and spacing, annotated IA for engineers, accessibility checklist, and a short usability test report.
acceptance_criteria: New surface map (SVG + annotated JSON list) reviewed and approved by PM and Eng leads
High-fidelity prototype demonstrates common flows: workspace switch, open rollout canary, cost drilldown < 3 clicks
Icon set (16/24/32px) created and added to Figma library with tokens and alt text specs
Accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation checks documented and pass internal a11y baseline
Handoff packet (Figma links, token exports, implementation checklist) uploaded and linked in ticket

comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Patel: Initial sketches uploaded. Two directions emerged: 'compact chip rail' vs 'zoned rail with persistent actions'. Compact favors density; zoned favors discoverability. Leaning toward zoned for first pass due to rollout controls needing persistent affordances.

2026-02-24 - Riley Zhang: Feedback from eng sync: zoned rail adds 8-12px to global width but enables sticky rollout toolbar which reduces micro-navigation. Concern: token changes may ripple; request explicit token map for spacing and icon sizes.

2026-03-07 - Usability lead (Nora Li): Quick test of prototype v1: participants located cost view in 2.3 avg clicks, rollout controls in 1.6 clicks. Feedback: workspace avatars should show tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with small badge. Recommend adding hover preview for workspace contents.

2026-03-09 - Riley Zhang: Updated hi-fi with badges and hover preview. Submitted for review. Noted trade-off: hover previews add hover surface complexity on mobile; we will use long-press on mobile per PM guidance.
2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Seeking design review approval from Angela Park and Eng leads. Also requested accessibility pass for contrast and keyboard nav from A11y team. Marking ticket In Review.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Primary trade-off considered: denser rail (more items visible) vs zoned rail (clearer affordances for rollouts/cost). We selected zoned rail to prioritize operational discoverability for enterprise users. Cost: small increase in horizontal footprint and more complex responsive rules. Mitigations: compressed icons at narrow widths, collapse to 'compact mode' on small screens, and long-press for mobile previews.
